summary: Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle (1927–1997) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sera and Gyuto Monasteries and Trashichöling under Ngawang Yönten and Tsadru Ngawang Losang. He held professorships at Minzu University and Tibet University (~1985–1997).

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist who studied at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He held professorships at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College, and Sanskrit College and University (1952).
Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He pursued his studies under R. K. Dikshit, Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi, and doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri.
Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was an Indologist and historian who completed his studies at Presidency University (~1957–1961), the University of Calcutta, and Patna University.
Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at SOAS University of London, completed a PhD at UCLouvain (until 2018), and served as a research scholar at UCLouvain.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche (born 1964) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenpo Rinchen, and served as professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University in 1990.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (born 1965), working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University under Dilgo Khyentse and others. He directed the Nitartha Institute and served at Kamalashila Institute.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse (born 1961) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London under Dilgo Khyentse, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, the 16th Karmapa, and Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.

Dörte Kamarid is a scholar in Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, completing an MA under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher.

E. E. Evans-Pritchard (1902–1973) studied at the University of Oxford (Exeter College) and the London School of Economics. He held academic posts at the London School of Economics, Cairo University, Cambridge, and Oxford (1946–1970).

E. Gene Smith (1936–2010) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the universities of Utah, Washington, and Leiden under Turrell V. Wylie and Dezhung Rinpoche, he held positions at the Library of Congress and the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

E. J. Rapson (1861–1937) was an Indologist and linguist educated at St John's College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1887–1906) and was Professor of Sanskrit at University College London (1903) and the University of Cambridge (~1906–1936).

E. Michael Mendelson (1928–2024) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his education at the University of Cambridge (King's College), the University of Paris (~1951–1953), and the University of Chicago (~1953–1956).

E. W. Adikaram (1905–1985) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he was principal at Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Eberhard Fischer (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who earned his PhD at the University of Basel. He served as director of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and later as president of the Rietberg-Gesellschaft.

Eberhard Sandschneider (born 1955) is a Sinologist who studied at Saarland University. He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and the German Council on Foreign Relations as Otto-Wolff-Direktor (2003–2016).

Eberhard Schrader (1836–1908) was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held professorial posts at the universities of Zurich, Giessen, Jena, and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).

Edeltraud Harzer is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Charles University and the University of Washington, and under Shrinarayan Mishra. She has held posts at Stanford, Indiana University, and the University of Texas at Austin (1998).

Edgar H. Sturtevant (1875–1952) was a linguist who completed his education at Illinois College and Indiana University. He held major academic appointments at Columbia University (~1908–1920) and Yale University (~1923–1943).

Edith Wyschogrod (1930–2009) was a philosopher and scholar of religious studies who completed her BA at Hunter College and her PhD at Columbia University. From 1992 to 2002, she was a professor at Rice University.
